parallel.requirements: Parallel recognized the core requirements: Rust 2021, zero external crates, std::env::args parsing, exact C++ output formatting, Cargo project layout with /output/test10.rs, no C++ library source reading, and byte-exact reference comparison.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed the reference binary, then split work between an implementation child owning the Rust project and a corpus child owning reference outputs and a verifier; the parent retained final cross-check and closure ownership.
parallel.implementation: The implementation child wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, a detailed src/earcut.rs port, and test10.rs with C atoi semantics, f64 math matching the source, no dependencies, and output without a final newline.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Only the implementation child wrote the required /output deliverables, while the corpus child wrote /tmp/ref10 verification artifacts; the parent later ran the corpus verifier against /output/target/release/test10 and reported the final layout.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included the implementation child's 25-case byte-exact comparison, direct diff checks, standalone rustc confirmation, no-warning rebuild, and the parent's later 30-case independent corpus verifier.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evident at closure; the official completed evaluator passed all 37 cases.

serial.requirements: Serial recognized the same Rust 2021, zero-dependency, exact CLI parsing, byte-output, Cargo layout, black-box, and compilation requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned all stages directly: reference probing, implementation, file writes, build, verification, and final response, with no child delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/geometry.rs, src/earcut.rs, and test10.rs, using an atoi-like parser and a compact outer-ring triangulation tailored to the observed constant index output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All serial deliverables were written in one sequence in /output and built into target/release/test10 plus a direct rustc binary, with no inter-agent merge step.
serial.verification: Serial built with Cargo and direct rustc, then compared reference and Rust outputs byte-for-byte across no-arg, positive, zero, negative, invalid, whitespace, plus-sign, and suffix cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evident at closure; the official completed evaluator passed all 37 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved the required Cargo layout, Rust 2021, std-only constraint, std::env::args parsing, exact formatting, and black-box reference behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial preserved the same required layout, parser, formatting, dependency, and black-box constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected correctness; parallel encoded a broader known invariant and serial inferred a smaller observed behavior set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated implementation to agent-0 and reference corpus construction to agent-1 while the parent owned final cross-verification and reporting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, implementation, building, verification, and final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit multi-agent ownership but no missing owner; serial avoided ownership boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child received a detailed brief with required output behavior, parser edge cases, Cargo layout, and expected verification; the corpus child received a separate verifier contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent carried all context locally and did not need handoffs or cross-agent interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child briefs and handoffs, but the contracts were adequate and their results were compatible when consumed by the parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation used a fuller earcut-style port with linked nodes, hole elimination behavior, fallbacks, and z-order hashing path, plus test10.rs parsing and output code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implementation used geometry generation plus a compact outer-ring ear-clipping traversal matching the observed reference behavior for this test.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented a broader algorithmic model; serial implemented a narrower task-specific model. Both produced accepted behavior for the official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both children completed and returned summaries; the parent received the implementation summary and corpus summary before running a parent-level verification step.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded directly from writes to build, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required result retrieval and use, which happened successfully; serial had no join risk because all work stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child owned the /output project files; the corpus child wrote only /tmp/ref10 artifacts, and the parent later used those artifacts to test the delivered binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote all /output source files and build artifacts itself, so there was no shared implementation workspace across agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared filesystem access but no concrete overwrite or incompatible merge; serial had no inter-agent shared-state exposure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified through child-local 25-case comparisons, direct diff and rustc checks, zero warning check, a parent-run 30-case corpus verifier, and official 37/37 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified by building with Cargo and rustc and running byte comparisons over representative argument cases before official 37/37 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader and had a parent-level independent check; serial verification was narrower but still sufficient for official acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more time and tokens because it ran two child tasks and an extra parent verifier, but the agent completed without timeout and left remaining provider budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed much faster with fewer tool calls and no subagent overhead, also without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive but not budget-failed or deadline-constrained; serial was leaner. The budget difference did not create an adverse process consequence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed evaluations: both modes passed all 37 official test cases. The task-solving difference is that parallel decomposed the work into implementation and reference-corpus children and then integrated their outputs through a parent-run verifier, while serial directly wrote and verified a smaller task-specific solution in one trajectory. The difference changed cost and implementation breadth, not acceptance.
parallel_contributors: Implementation child produced the final Cargo project and target/release/test10.
Reference-corpus child produced a 30-case verifier that the parent used before final response.
serial_contributors: Single actor implemented a compact outer-ring triangulation and local geometry module.
Single actor built with Cargo and rustc and compared representative reference outputs.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented a broader earcut-style algorithm; serial implemented a smaller behavior-specific triangulation, but both matched official tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy contrast only
